claims.text: The targeted material family is fcc high-entropy alloys derived from the Fe-Co-Ni system, such as FeCoNi and FeCoNiCr.
The primary properties targeted for improvement are mechanical stability, stacking-fault energy, and phase stability.
Stacking-fault energy and phase stability are critically dependent on the magnetic state.
Conventional static DFT predicts zero or negligible magnetic moments for Co, Ni, and Cr in these alloys.
Static DFT fails to capture significant orbital and spin contributions arising from finite-temperature longitudinal spin fluctuations.
Neglecting these magnetic contributions produces inaccurate predictions of the fcc-hcp transition temperature and the sign of the stacking-fault energy.
At 100 K, LSF modeling yields magnetic moments of approximately 0.73 μB for Co and 0.24 μB for Ni.
LSFs induce sizable finite magnetic moments on Co, Cr, and Ni over the investigated temperature and volume ranges.
The LSF-induced moments significantly alter magnetic entropy and internal-energy contributions to free energy.
At low temperatures, magnetic effects stabilize hcp or produce negative stacking-fault energy.
Negative low-temperature stacking-fault energy promotes deformation twinning or nanotwinning.
At increasing temperature, magneto-volume coupling causes stacking-fault energy to rise monotonically and suppresses hcp formation.
The stacking-fault energy is predicted to range from about -15 to 2 mJ m⁻² between 77 and 293 K.
The stacking-fault energy is predicted to rise to approximately 31 mJ m⁻² at 1000 K.
Accounting for LSFs predicts an fcc-hcp transition temperature of approximately 430 K.
The predicted transition temperature is lower than a floating-spin prediction of approximately 438 K and an experimental value of approximately 633 K.
The discrepancy between the predicted and experimental transition temperatures is due to omitted phonon effects.
The orbital moment contribution driven by LSFs is the key factor enabling tunable stacking-fault-energy behavior.
Optimizing the Fe-Co-Ni composition to maximize the LSF-induced magnetic contribution will enhance cryogenic ductility and toughness while retaining elevated-temperature stability.
The proposed mechanism may not transfer to refractory BCC HEAs or alloys in which ordering or high Al content quenches magnetic moments.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis repeatedly identifies an orbital-moment contribution as the central challenge and driver, whereas the mediator and mechanism describe only induced magnetic or spin moments and never distinguish or calculate orbital moments.
